LZM is a higher-relevance underfollowed candidate because Kabanga offers ex-Indonesia nickel optionality plus hydrometallurgical processing exposure; later layers must verify financing, permitting, capex, and offtake.
CNIKF belongs in the speculative_shadow lane as a US-traded non-Indonesian nickel-sulphide development candidate; survival depends on financing, permitting, and market-cap/liquidity checks.

Sulfuric acid may be a parallel HPAL bottleneck tied to Indonesia nickel; HWKN is only a second-order US chemical-distribution proxy and requires evidence of pricing or volume sensitivity before promotion.

node: Indonesia nickel export routing, resource nationalism, and HPAL supply-chain exposure
summary: Layer 1B expanded the universe around the regulation/logistics/working-capital chokepoint rather than only physical nickel mining. The strongest reference anchor is Vale because PT Vale Indonesia is a direct Indonesian nickel producer. The underfollowed lane points to non-Indonesian nickel-development alternatives and second-order HPAL input exposure: Lifezone Metals for Tanzania nickel plus hydrometallurgical processing, Canada Nickel for Canadian nickel-sulphide restart/development optionality, and Hawkins for sulfuric-acid distribution exposure tied to HPAL feedstock constraints. These are research candidates only; the Indonesia export-rule inclusion of nickel and direct contract impacts still require primary-source verification.
